question: With which substance does silver react and turn black?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Sulphur**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Silver reacts with sulphur or sulphur-containing compounds in the air to form silver sulphide (Ag2S), which is black in color.
 
• This reaction is known as tarnishing, which commonly affects silverware and jewelry.
 
• The formation of silver sulphide is a chemical change where silver (Ag) reacts with hydrogen sulphide (H2S) or other sulphur compounds.
 
• Tarnishing can be accelerated in environments with high levels of pollution or humidity, as these conditions often contain more sulphur compounds.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Silver Sulphide (Ag2S)**

 
 
• Silver sulphide is a black compound that forms when silver reacts with sulphur or hydrogen sulphide.
 
• This reaction is a common cause of tarnish on silver items, making them appear dull and blackened.
 
• Silver sulphide is insoluble in water and is often removed by polishing or using chemical dips designed for silver cleaning.
 
 
 
• **Tarnishing**
 
 
• Tarnishing is a chemical process that occurs when a metal reacts with a non-metal compound, resulting in a thin layer of corrosion on the metal's surface.
 
• In the case of silver, tarnishing occurs due to the formation of silver sulphide from the reaction with sulphur compounds in the air.
 
• Preventive measures include storing silver in airtight containers, using anti-tarnish strips, and regularly cleaning the silver items.
 
 
 
• **Hydrogen Sulphide (H2S)**
 
 
• Hydrogen sulphide is a colorless, poisonous, and flammable gas with the characteristic foul odor of rotten eggs.
 
• It is commonly found in volcanic gases, natural gas, and some mineral springs.
 
• In the atmosphere, hydrogen sulphide can react with silver to form silver sulphide, leading to tarnishing.
